name: Characterization Fundamentals & Metallography
summary: Introduces how materials are examined and measured: sample preparation, optical microscopy, quantitative microstructure and good experimental practice.

topics.name: The characterization toolbox: what each family of techniques reveals (structure, chemistry, properties)
Probes and signals: photons, electrons, ions and neutrons interacting with matter
Sample preparation: sectioning, mounting, grinding, polishing and etching
Optical (light) microscopy: resolution, contrast modes, polarised light and DIC
Quantitative metallography and stereology: grain size, phase fraction, particle size
Density, porosity and chemical analysis basics (Archimedes, ICP, combustion analysis)
Measurement uncertainty, error propagation and calibration
Statistics for materials data: distributions, confidence intervals, regression and Weibull plots
Design of experiments for materials development
Laboratory safety, notebooks and reporting results
